_comment: Stingray Crash Analyzer - crash pattern library. SECTIONS: (1) builtin_patterns - overrides for the 60 code-level pattern messages by ID. Only 11 most-commonly-customized patterns are listed here; add others by ID to override. Set enabled:false to fall back to code default. (2) patterns - custom matchable patterns with match criteria. NOTE: SIG-HD2-SSR-01 and SIG-HD2-VTC-01 are handled by code-level CRASH_SIGNATURES (more precise match functions) and are NOT duplicated here to avoid redundant reporting. LUA_MOD_DETECTED is generated dynamically by the code and is not available for JSON override.

_format.id: Unique identifier - must match what the code expects for builtin patterns
_format.name: Short crash name shown in the UI
fix: Step 1
Step 2
Step 3
_format.enabled: true to enable, false to disable

_match_fields_documentation.ex_param_0: Exception parameter[0] as hex string or int. For 0xC0000005: 0=READ, 1=WRITE, 8=EXECUTE
_match_fields_documentation.fault_addr_min: Minimum faulting address (param[1]) as hex string or int
_match_fields_documentation.fault_addr_max: Maximum faulting address (param[1]) as hex string or int. Set min=max for exact match
_match_fields_documentation.is_suicide: true/false - whether the engine suicide pattern was detected
_match_fields_documentation.crash_mod_contains: Substring to match in the crash module name (case-insensitive)
_match_fields_documentation.crash_offset: Exact hex offset of the crash address within its module (e.g. '0x79A553')
_match_fields_documentation.stack_contains: Substring to match in stack frame module names (case-insensitive)
_match_fields_documentation.stack_contains_depth: Max stack depth to search for stack_contains (default 9999)
_match_fields_documentation.module_loaded: Module name that must be loaded (case-insensitive substring match)
_match_fields_documentation.module_not_loaded: Module name that must NOT be loaded (case-insensitive substring match)
_match_fields_documentation.active_thread_mod_contains: Substring to match in active thread module names
_match_fields_documentation.lua_mod_present: true/false - whether Lua mods are detected
_match_fields_documentation.null_register: Register name (string) or list of register names that must be null at crash. e.g. 'R13' or ['RAX','RBP']
_match_fields_documentation.call_chain_offset: Object {module, offset} - check if this offset appears in the reconstructed call chain
_match_fields_documentation.call_chain_offset_repeat: Object {module, offset, min_count} - check if this offset appears min_count+ times in the call chain (recursion detection)

builtin_patterns.name: Engine suicide during DirectStorage streaming
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected an internal error while loading assets via DirectStorage and shut itself down. This is often caused by outdated GPU drivers that don't properly support DirectStorage.
fix: Update your GPU drivers to the latest version
If on AMD: use DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) to fully clean old drivers first
Verify game files through Steam
If the crash persists, disable DirectStorage
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Engine suicide with active DStorage thread - likely DS decompression or IO error

builtin_patterns.name: Engine suicide from Lua scripting error
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected a scripting error and shut itself down. This can be caused by mods that modify game scripts, or a bug in a game update.
fix: If you have mods installed, remove them and try again
Verify game files through Steam
Check the game log file for a Lua error message
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Engine suicide with active Lua thread - check Lua stack and recent script changes

builtin_patterns.name: Engine suicide during audio playback
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected an error in the audio system and shut itself down. This can happen with certain audio devices or driver configurations.
fix: Try setting your audio output to stereo instead of surround sound
Update your audio drivers
Try disabling audio enhancements in Windows sound settings
Check the game log for audio error messages
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Engine suicide with active Wwise thread - check audio event / bank loading

builtin_patterns.name: Engine suicide during GPU rendering
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected an error in the graphics system and shut itself down. This is most commonly caused by outdated or unstable GPU drivers, or a GPU hardware issue.
fix: Update your GPU drivers to the latest version
If overclocking your GPU, revert to stock settings
Try lowering graphics settings
Check GPU temperature - overheating can cause this
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Engine suicide with active D3D12/GPU driver thread - device lost or driver timeout

builtin_patterns.name: Engine detected an internal error and shut down
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected something unexpected internally and safely shut itself down rather than continuing in a broken state. The engine log file contains the actual error message.
fix: Check the .log file next to the .dmp for the real error
Verify game files through Steam
Share the .log AND .dmp files with the dev team
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Generic engine suicide - check engine log for trigger

builtin_patterns.name: GPU driver crashed
builtin_patterns.player_message: The graphics driver crashed inside the game. This is almost always a driver bug or hardware issue, not a game bug.
fix: Update your GPU drivers to the latest version
Use DDU (Display Driver Uninstaller) to fully clean old drivers first
If overclocking your GPU or VRAM, revert to stock settings
Check GPU temperature under load
If on a laptop, make sure the game is using the dedicated GPU, not the integrated one
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Crash inside GPU driver DLL - not engine code

builtin_patterns.name: GPU error: device lost / stopped responding
builtin_patterns.player_message: The GPU stopped responding to the game. This is almost always a driver, hardware, or overheating issue - not a game bug.
fix: Update GPU drivers
Check GPU temperature - use HWiNFO64 or GPU-Z while gaming
Revert any GPU overclock
If the problem persists, run a GPU stress test (FurMark) to check hardware stability

builtin_patterns.name: Stack overflow
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game ran out of call stack space. This is a game bug, not a hardware issue. It typically means a function called itself too many times in a loop.
fix: This is a game bug - please report it with the dump file
Note exactly what you were doing in-game when it crashed
Check if it happens consistently in the same situation
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Stack overflow - look for infinite recursion in the crashing thread

builtin_patterns.name: Memory corruption detected
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game detected that its memory was corrupted. This is a game bug. It can be hard to reproduce consistently because the corruption may happen before the crash.
fix: This is a game bug - please report it with the dump file
Note what you were doing when it crashed - especially any unusual sequences of actions
If you have mods, try without them first
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Heap corruption - use heap debug allocator to find the stomper

builtin_patterns.name: Crash with mods detected
builtin_patterns.player_message: Mods were detected in this crash. Mods can cause crashes that wouldn't otherwise occur. Before reporting this as a game bug, please verify the crash happens without mods installed.
fix: Remove all mods and verify the crash still happens
If the crash goes away without mods, the mod is the cause
If it still crashes without mods, please share the new dump with the dev team
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Mods detected - verify crash is reproducible in vanilla before investigation

builtin_patterns.name: Unhandled game error
builtin_patterns.player_message: The game encountered an internal error it didn't know how to handle. This is a game bug. Check the engine log for the error message.
fix: Check the .log file next to the .dmp for the error message
Share both the .log and .dmp with the dev team
Note what you were doing when it crashed
builtin_patterns.dev_note: Unhandled C++ exception - check exception type and message in log

patterns.name: Helldivers 2 Guard page violation in EAC-injected code
patterns.player_message: Code running in private executable memory (injected by EasyAntiCheat or JIT-compiled) tried to read from a system DLL that was protected by a guard page. This is an EAC-domain crash: the game's own code was not at fault. The root cause is unclear without the engine log.
fix: Verify game files in Steam (this covers EAC files).
If the crash recurs, try reinstalling EAC separately (run the EAC installer in the game's binaries folder).
Report to Arrowhead with the dump and engine log (--log-to-file). Include: 0x80000001 guard page violation, RIP in private exec memory, accessed address in D3D12.dll.
patterns.dev_note: SIG-HD2-GPV-01 (open): 0x80000001 STATUS_GUARD_PAGE_VIOLATION. RIP in PRIVATE EXECUTABLE memory (not any loaded module). READ access to an address inside a system DLL (typically D3D12.dll). EAC-captured dump. Multiple null/near-null registers. Stack smashed. This is an EAC-domain crash: could be EAC hook code faulting on a guard page, or tamper detection triggering.

patterns.name: Helldivers 2 Execute PE header (RIP redirected to a module's base +0x0)
patterns.player_message: The CPU was redirected to the very start of a DLL (the PE file header, which is data, not executable code) and tried to execute it. The CPU then faulted because PE header pages are read-only and non-executable. The most likely cause is a corrupted indirect call target (a vtable slot or function pointer holding a module's base address), but the exact source of the corruption has not yet been confirmed.
fix: This is an engine bug: no user-side fix is confirmed.
Capture the engine log (--log-to-file) and report to Arrowhead with the dump.
Include in the report: EXECUTE-violation at a module's base address (+0x0), the module name (runtime.dll in all known cases), and the build identifier.
patterns.dev_note: SIG-HD2-PEHDR-01 (open): 0xC0000005 EXECUTE (param[0]=0x8) at a loaded module's base address (offset +0x0 = PE header). The CPU was redirected to the MZ/PE header bytes (read-only data) and faulted on NX. Cross-case fingerprint = {0xC0000005, EXECUTE, crash_offset=0x0, module=runtime.dll}. MECHANISM (HYPOTHESIS, unconfirmed): corrupted indirect call target (vtable slot or function pointer) holding a module base address. The RDX=0xE0670103 observation in one case (the CRT exception code for STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) supports heap corruption as the upstream cause but does not prove it. runtime.dll STATIC ANALYSIS: the DLL is 64 MB, Authenticode-signed by Arrowhead Game Studios AB (genuine/untampered), and HEAVILY PACKED (custom packer: 12 sections including .rwx (RWX), no .text section, ~50 MB of virtualized code; no VMProtect/Themida/Enigma/UPX string signatures). Export directory is EMPTY (no exports). RVA +0x0 is just the MZ/PE header -- NOT a deliberate crash stub. EXCLUDED HYPOTHESIS: 'runtime.dll +0x0 is a deliberate self-trap analogous to preloader.dll+0xB010' is REJECTED -- no trap section at +0x0, no export pointing at +0x0, AddressOfEntryPoint is elsewhere, bytes at +0x0 are just MZ header data. The packer does have anti-tamper timing checks (KUSER_SHARED_DATA TickCount) and obfuscated control flow, but none redirect execution to +0x0. STRENGTHENED CONCLUSION: the self-trap-at-+0x0 hypothesis is rejected; upstream heap corruption remains the most plausible explanation. Build: 42899.41204.

patterns.name: Helldivers 2 Null pointer dereference at struct field offset
patterns.player_message: The game tried to access a field of an object that was null (destroyed, never initialized, or returned null by a function that wasn't checked). This is a game bug: the code didn't validate the object before using it.
fix: This is a game bug: report it with the dump file.
Note what you were doing when it crashed (loading a mission, opening a menu, joining a squad, etc.).
Capture the engine log (--log-to-file) for more context on what the engine was doing.
patterns.dev_note: SIG-HD2-NPD-01 (open): 0xC0000005 READ at a near-null address (typically 0x58 = field offset +88). The null object pointer was in RAX. The faulting instruction did [RAX+offset]. This is the most common crash type in C++ engines: a null 'this' pointer or unchecked function return. Note: if the crash offset is +0x9F60ED, the code-level signature SIG-HD2-AVND-01 (audio voice null-deref) takes precedence and provides a specific fix (remove virtual audio devices). Build: 42899.41204.

patterns.name: Helldivers 2 Use-after-free with deep recursion
patterns.player_message: The game entered a deep recursion (15+ re-entries of the same function), which culminated in a use-after-free: a pointer to freed memory was dereferenced. This is a game bug involving both unbounded recursion and a stale pointer.
fix: This is a game bug: report it with the dump file.
Note what you were doing when it crashed.
Capture the engine log (--log-to-file).
Include in the report: the recursion hub offset and the UAF faulting address.
patterns.dev_note: SIG-HD2-UAF-01 (open): 0xC0000005 READ at a heap address (valid-looking pointer to freed memory). Deep recursion (x15-18 re-entries) in helldivers2.exe precedes the crash. The recursion may cause stack pressure leading to premature object cleanup, which then causes the UAF. Build: 42899.41204. Recursion hub offset varies by code path.

patterns.name: D3D11 + RDNA GPU crash at helldivers2.exe+0x537C92
patterns.player_message: This crash matches a known, reproducible bug that occurs when running the game in DirectX 11 on AMD RDNA-generation GPUs (RX 5000/6000/7000 series). It has been confirmed on multiple separate crash reports, all hitting the exact same instruction and call stack inside the game's renderer.
fix: Switch the game to DirectX 12 - remove any '--use-d3d11' Steam launch option if one is set, or otherwise force the renderer back to D3D12

If you need D3D11 for a specific reason (e.g. an overlay/capture tool that doesn't support D3D12), be aware this is a known incompatibility with RDNA GPUs in this game and there is currently no other workaround besides switching back to D3D12

Report this crash address (helldivers2.exe+0x537C92) to the development team if you have a build/version where this is supposed to be fixed and it still occurs - the offset will differ between game versions, so confirm against the version this dump was captured on
patterns.dev_note: Confirmed via two independently captured dumps with byte-for-byte identical exception code (0xC0000005), exception params (['0x0','0x3']), and the full 12-frame call chain (helldivers2.exe+0x537C92 -> +0x660265 -> +0x1A11930 -> +0x626A46 -> +0x1EC2E3 -> +0x168E898 -> +0x1B11390 -> +0x168AFA8 -> +0x708453 -> +0x626A46 -> +0x625748 -> +0x166B8F0). Both dumps confirmed AMD RDNA driver-store DLLs present (amdxx64.dll/amdenc64.dll/amdihk64.dll) and D3D11 active (one via explicit --use-d3d11 Steam launch option). User-reported pattern: multiple testers with RDNA GPUs (6700XT confirmed) reproduce this reliably under D3D11; not yet confirmed whether non-RDNA AMD or Nvidia GPUs hit the same offset under D3D11, or whether RDNA GPUs under D3D12 are unaffected (cannot force-generate a 'successful, no-crash' dump for comparison). The crash_offset is build-specific and WILL need updating if this is checked against a different helldivers2.exe version/timestamp than the two source dumps.

patterns.name: Helldivers 2 Use-after-free in GPU/rendering path (helldivers2.exe +0xD96DDC)
patterns.player_message: The game crashed because it tried to read through a pointer to memory that had already been freed. This is a use-after-free bug in the game's rendering or GPU-related code. The pointer was valid at some point but the object it pointed to was freed or moved, and the game didn't clear the pointer before using it again.
fix: This is a game bug: no user-side fix is confirmed.
Update your GPU drivers to the latest version (a driver bug may contribute to the timing that triggers this).
Try lowering graphics settings or disabling features like FSR/frame generation to reduce GPU-driver interaction complexity.
Capture the engine log (--log-to-file) and report to Arrowhead with the dump.
Include in the report: crash offset +0xD96DDC, the faulting heap address, the GPU model, and the driver version.
patterns.dev_note: SIG-HD2-UAF02-01 (open): 0xC0000005 READ at a heap address (large, not near-null) in helldivers2.exe +0xD96DDC. The faulting address is in the heap region but NOT in any captured memory range, indicating the memory was freed before the read. RAX holds a heap pointer (also freed/invalid at crash time). Call chain includes GPU driver callback (nvwgf2umx.dll on stack in one case) and runtime.dll +0x4D0000 (the known stack-smash sentinel). This is a use-after-free in the game's GPU/rendering path. Build: 42899.41204.

_code_signatures._comment: These signatures are matched in code via match_signatures() and reported in the CRASH SIGNATURE MATCH section. They are NOT in patterns[] to avoid duplicate reporting. They use more complex match functions than JSON patterns support.

signatures.title: Helldivers 2 Stingray Setup Recursion
signatures.fix: RCX=0 (or RAX=0): clean reinstall. RCX not null: clear shader cache and delete user_settings.config.
signatures.match_criteria: 0xC0000005 in helldivers2.exe, +0x170xxxx recursion region (>=2 frames). RCX=0 → reinstall, RCX≠0 → shader cache.

signatures.title: Helldivers 2 EXECUTE at KUSER_SHARED_DATA range (R13=0, stack smashed)
signatures.fix: No confirmed fix. Report to Arrowhead with dump + engine log. Source of corruption not yet identified (hypothesis: corrupted indirect call target).

signatures.title: Helldivers 2 RefcountedPackageSystem reference map overflow
signatures.fix: No user-side fix. Try changing loadout or clearing cloud save. Report to Arrowhead.

signatures.title: Helldivers 2 shader/settings corruption triggering engine init recursion
signatures.fix: Clear shader cache and delete user_settings.config. (Now handled by SSR-01 via RCX check - SCS-01 catches low-sentinel cases that SSR-01 misses.)
signatures.match_criteria: 0xC0000005 in helldivers2.exe, +0x170xxxx recursion (<3 sentinels, distinguishes from SSR-01)

signatures.title: Helldivers 2 Audio voice null-deref during voice list iteration
signatures.fix: Remove all virtual audio devices (VB-Cable, VoiceMeeter, Meta Quest link, VirtualBox audio). Set default audio output to a single stable device (wired speakers or headphones, not Bluetooth). Disable unused audio endpoints in Windows Sound settings.
signatures.match_criteria: 0xC0000005 READ at 0x58, helldivers2.exe+0x9F60ED, RAX=0. RCX varies (voice list index, e.g. 0x15 or 0x21).

_builtin_pattern_registry._comment: All 60 builtin pattern IDs in the code. Add any of these to builtin_patterns[] to override their messages. Only 11 are listed by default (the most commonly customized).
